sites.evidence_type: topology inference (C-terminal snorkel — no accessible terminus)
sites.rationale: C-terminus not extracellular (topology 'I' at residue L) and no accessible N-terminus — C-terminal snorkel presents the tag on the surface via a TM-snorkeling linker (fallback: no natively accessible terminus)

literature_notes: All eleven ledger lines (L1–L11) describe tags appended to the C-terminus of FLVCR2 (mouse Flvcr2-HA knock-in, L1–L9; human FLVCR2-GFP in Xenopus oocytes, L10–L11). The authoritative topology landmarks place the C-terminus within the intracellular region 488–526; residue 526 (L) is cytoplasmic. Consequently, every cited tag is on the intracellular face and none qualifies as an extracellular surface tag site. The N-terminus (residues 1–85) is also intracellular. No ledger line reports any insertion in an extracellular loop or at an extracellular terminus of this protein. Zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA tag (with G4S linker) appended after residue 526 of endogenous mouse Flvcr2; topology places residue 526 in the intracellular region 488–526, so this is a cytoplasmic tag, not an extracellular surface tag. Homozygous knock-in mice showed no effect on fertility or health (L2), confirming functional tolerance, but the tag faces the cytoplasm.

C-terminal GFP fusion on human FLVCR2 expressed in Xenopus oocytes; confocal microscopy confirmed plasma-membrane localisation (L11), but the GFP is appended after residue 526 which is intracellular per topology — this validates surface trafficking, not an extracellular tag.
